results.title: 2-CNF formulas
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A CNF formula is a 2-CNF formula when each of its clauses, viewed as a list of literals, has length at most $2$ (repeated literals are counted with multiplicity).

results.title: Complement of a literal
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: The complement of a literal $(x, b)$, with variable index $x \in \mathbb{N}$ and polarity $b$, is the literal $(x, \lnot b)$: same variable, opposite polarity.

results.title: Clauses with at most two literals
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: In a clause with at most two literals, any two different members $a$ and $b$ are all of its members: every member $c$ of the clause equals $a$ or $b$.

results.title: Implication edge
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a CNF formula $\varphi$ and literals $l$ and $m$, there is an implication edge from $l$ to $m$ when some clause of $\varphi$ contains both $\neg l$ and $m$, either as two different literals or with $m$ as its only literal (so a unit clause $m$ gives the edge from $\neg m$ to $m$).

results.title: Reachability in the implication graph
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a CNF formula $\varphi$, a literal $l$ reaches a literal $m$ when there is a path of zero or more implication edges of $\varphi$ from $l$ to $m$; that is, reachability is the reflexive-transitive closure of the implication edge relation.

results.title: Skew symmetry of the implication graph
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a CNF formula $\varphi$ and literals $l$ and $m$, if the implication graph of $\varphi$ has an edge from $l$ to $m$, then it also has the contrapositive edge from $\lnot m$ to $\lnot l$, where $\lnot$ denotes the complementary literal.

results.title: Satisfying assignments respect implication edges
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a 2-CNF formula and $\sigma$ an assignment of truth values to the variables that satisfies $\varphi$. If the implication graph of $\varphi$ has an edge from a literal $l$ to a literal $m$ and $\sigma$ satisfies $l$, then $\sigma$ satisfies $m$.

results.title: Resolution invariant of the implication graph
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A clause $C$ satisfies the invariant with respect to a CNF formula $\varphi$ when for every literal $a$ of $C$ there is a literal $b$ of $C$ such that the complementary literal $\lnot a$ reaches $b$ in the implication graph of $\varphi$ (by a path of zero or more edges).

results.title: Resolution refutations give contradictory cycles
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If a CNF formula $\varphi$ does not contain the empty clause and the empty clause is derivable from $\varphi$ by resolution, then there is a variable $x$ such that the literals $x$ and $\neg x$ reach each other in the implication graph of $\varphi$.

results.title: 2-SAT characterization
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: 2-SAT characterization (Aspvall, Plass, Tarjan): a 2-CNF formula is satisfiable iff it has no empty clause and no variable `x` such that `x` and `¬x` reach each other in the implication graph.

results.title: Literals over the variables of a formula
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: For a CNF formula $\varphi$, a literal over $\varphi$ is a pair $(x, b)$ of a variable index $x \in \mathbb{N}$ and a polarity $b \in \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$ such that the variable $x$ occurs in $\varphi$. These literals are the vertices of the implication graph of $\varphi$.

results.title: Complement of a literal over a formula
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a CNF formula $\varphi$, the complement of a literal $(x, b)$ over the variables of $\varphi$ is the literal $(x, \lnot b)$, which is again a literal over the variables of $\varphi$.

results.title: Duplicate-free list of the variables of a CNF formula
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a CNF formula $\varphi$, this is the list of the variables occurring in the literals of $\varphi$, each exactly once, in the order of their last occurrences when the clauses of $\varphi$ and their literals are read from first to last.

results.title: List of the literals of a CNF formula
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a CNF formula $\varphi$, this is the list of all literals over the variables of $\varphi$, each appearing exactly once, arranged variable by variable: for each variable $x$ of $\varphi$, the positive literal $(x, \mathrm{true})$ is immediately followed by the negative literal $(x, \mathrm{false})$.

results.title: Successors in the implication graph
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a CNF formula and $l$ a literal over the variables of $\varphi$, and write $\neg l$ for the complementary literal. The successors of $l$ are the literals $m$ over the variables of $\varphi$ such that the implication graph of $\varphi$ has an edge from $l$ to $m$: some clause of $\varphi$ contains $\neg l$ and $m$, either as two different literals or as its only literal. They are listed without…

results.title: Adjacency table of the implication graph
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a CNF formula $\varphi$, the hash map that sends each literal over the variables of $\varphi$ to the list of its implication-graph successors, that is, of the literals $m$ over the variables of $\varphi$ with an implication edge from it to $m$.

results.title: Implication graph as a finite directed graph
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a CNF formula $\varphi$, the finite directed graph whose vertices are the literals over the variables of $\varphi$, listed without repetition, and whose out-neighbours of a literal $l$ are the literals $m$ over the variables of $\varphi$ with an implication edge from $l$ to $m$, read from the adjacency table of $\varphi$.

results.title: Implication edges end over variables of the formula
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a CNF formula $\varphi$ and literals $l$ and $m$, if the implication graph of $\varphi$ has an edge from $l$ to $m$, then the variable of $m$ occurs in $\varphi$.

results.title: Reachability in the finite implication graph
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a CNF formula $\varphi$ and literals $l$ and $m$ over the variables of $\varphi$, $m$ is reachable from $l$ in the implication graph of $\varphi$, viewed as a finite directed graph on these literals, if and only if $l$ reaches $m$ by implication edges of $\varphi$.

results.title: SCC-based 2-SAT decision procedure
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a CNF formula $\varphi$, the procedure returns false if $\varphi$ contains the empty clause; otherwise it returns true if and only if no block of the strongly connected components computed for the implication graph of $\varphi$ contains a literal together with its complementary literal.

results.title: A positive literal reaching its complement lies over a variable of the formula
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a CNF formula $\varphi$ and a variable $x$, if the positive literal $(x, \mathrm{true})$ reaches the negative literal $(x, \mathrm{false})$ in the implication graph of $\varphi$, then $x$ occurs in $\varphi$.

results.title: Correctness of the SCC-based 2-SAT procedure
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every CNF formula $\varphi$ in which every clause has at most two literals, the SCC-based 2-SAT decision procedure returns true on $\varphi$ if and only if $\varphi$ is satisfiable.

results.title: Product of the reduced incidence algebra
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\Omega$ be a set. For functions $f$ and $g$ from the finite subsets of $\Omega$ to $\mathbb{Q}$, their product $fg$ is the function on finite subsets given by $(fg)(X) = \sum_{Y \subseteq X} f(Y)\, g(X \setminus Y)$.

results.title: Elements of the reduced incidence algebra
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\Omega$ be a set. A function $f$ from the finite subsets of $\Omega$ to $\mathbb{Q}$ lies in the algebra $A = \bigoplus_n V_n$, where $V_n$ consists of the functions vanishing off the $n$-element subsets, when there is a natural number $N$ such that $f(X) = 0$ for every finite subset $X$ of $\Omega$ with more than $N$ elements.

results.title: Invariant functions on finite subsets
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $G$ be a group of permutations of a set $\Omega$. A function $f$ from the finite subsets of $\Omega$ to $\mathbb{Q}$ is $G$-invariant when $f(\sigma(X)) = f(X)$ for every $\sigma \in G$ and every finite subset $X$ of $\Omega$, where $\sigma(X)$ is the image of $X$ under $\sigma$.

results.title: Cameron's conjecture on invariant incidence algebras (Kourovka 13.29)

results.summary: The statement that for every infinite set $\Omega$ and every group $G$ of permutations of $\Omega$ all of whose orbits are infinite, the following holds: if $f$ and $g$ are nonzero functions from the finite subsets of $\Omega$ to $\mathbb{Q}$ that are $G$-invariant ($f(\sigma(X)) = f(X)$ for all $\sigma \in G$ and all finite $X$, and likewise for $g$) and that each vanish on all subsets of size larger than some…

results.title: Cameron's conjecture on invariant incidence algebras holds (Pouzet)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\Omega$ be an infinite set and let $G$ be a group of permutations of $\Omega$ all of whose orbits are infinite. Let $f$ and $g$ be nonzero functions from the finite subsets of $\Omega$ to $\mathbb{Q}$ that are $G$-invariant ($f(\sigma(X)) = f(X)$ for all $\sigma \in G$ and all finite $X$, and likewise for $g$) and that each vanish on all subsets of size larger than some bound. part.title: Modular inverses from the Euclidean algorithm

path: Modular inverses from the Euclidean algorithm

results.title: Least absolute inverse
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For integers $x$ and $a$ and a natural number $n$, $x$ is the least absolute inverse of $a$ modulo $n$ when $xa \equiv 1 \pmod{n}$ and $-n < 2x \le n$, that is, when $x$ is an inverse of $a$ modulo $n$ in the half-open interval $-n/2 < x \le n/2$.

results.title: Euclidean switching data
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A natural number $N$, a sequence $r_0, r_1, \dots$ of natural numbers and a sequence $s_0, s_1, \dots$ of integers form Euclidean switching data when $N \ge 1$; $r_0 > r_1 > \cdots > r_{N+1} = 1$, with $r_0, \dots, r_{N+1}$ all positive; for each $i = 1, \dots, N$ there is a positive integer $q_i$ with $r_{i-1} = q_i r_i + r_{i+1}$; $s_{N+1} = 1$; and $s_{i+1} r_{i-1} + s_i r_i = 1$ for each $i = 1, \dots, N$.

results.title: Bézout coefficients are modular inverses
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $m$ and $n$ be coprime positive integers, and let $x$ and $y$ be integers with $xm + yn = 1$. Then $xm \equiv 1 \pmod{n}$ and $yn \equiv 1 \pmod{m}$; that is, $x$ is an inverse of $m$ modulo $n$ and $y$ is an inverse of $n$ modulo $m$.

results.title: Modular inverse switching
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $m$ and $n$ be positive integers with $\gcd(m, n) = 1$, and let $t$ be an integer with $\gcd(|t|, n) = 1$. Then $m = kn + t$ for some integer $k$ if and only if there are integers $x$ and $y$ with $xt \equiv 1 \pmod{n}$, $yn \equiv 1 \pmod{m}$ and $xm + yn = 1$.

results.title: Least absolute inverses propagate down the Euclidean sequence
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $r_0, r_1, \ldots$ be natural numbers, $s_0, s_1, \ldots$ integers and $N \ge 1$ such that $(r, s, N)$ is Euclidean switching data: $r_0 > r_1 > \cdots > r_{N+1} = 1$ are the successive remainders of the Euclidean algorithm, $s_{N+1} = 1$, and $s_{i+1} r_{i-1} + s_i r_i = 1$ for $1 \le i \le N$. If $1 \le j \le N$ and $s_{j+1}$ is the least absolute inverse of $r_{j+1}$ modulo $r_j$, then $s_j$ is the least…

results.title: Every switching inverse is a least absolute inverse
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $(r_i)$, $(s_i)$ and $N$ be Euclidean switching data. Then for every $i$ with $1 \le i \le N + 1$, $s_i$ is the least absolute inverse of $r_i$ modulo $r_{i-1}$.

results.title: The Euclidean Bézout coefficients are least absolute inverses
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $m > n > 1$ be integers, write $g = \gcd(m, n)$, and let $(r_i)$, $(s_i)$ and $N$ be Euclidean switching data with $r_0 = m/g$ and $r_1 = n/g$. Then $s_2 m + s_1 n = g$, $s_2$ is the least absolute inverse of $m/g$ modulo $n/g$, and $s_1$ is the least absolute inverse of $n/g$ modulo $m/g$.

results.title: The Euclidean Bézout coefficients are smallest in absolute value
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $m > n > 1$ be integers, write $g = \gcd(m, n)$, and let $(r_i)$, $(s_i)$ and $N$ be Euclidean switching data with $r_0 = m/g$ and $r_1 = n/g$. Then for all integers $x$ and $y$ with $xm + yn = g$, we have $|s_2| \le |x|$ and $|s_1| \le |y|$.

results.title: Rankin's minimality of the Euclidean Bézout pair
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $m > n > 1$ be integers, write $g = \gcd(m, n)$, and let $(r_i)$, $(s_i)$ and $N$ be Euclidean switching data with $r_0 = m/g$ and $r_1 = n/g$. Then for all integers $x$ and $y$ with $xm + yn = g$, we have $s_2^2 + s_1^2 \le x^2 + y^2$.

results.title: Both first inverses extremal, odd–odd case
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $(r_i)$, $(s_i)$ and $N$ be Euclidean switching data with $r_0$ and $r_1$ both odd. Then $2|s_1| = r_0 - 1$ and $2|s_2| = r_1 - 1$ hold simultaneously if and only if $r_0 = r_1 + 2$.

results.title: Both first inverses extremal, odd–even case
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $(r_i)$, $(s_i)$ and $N$ be Euclidean switching data with $r_0$ odd and $r_1$ even. Then $2|s_1| = r_0 - 1$ and $2|s_2| = r_1$ hold simultaneously if and only if $r_1 = 2$.

results.title: First inverses not both extremal, even–odd case
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $(r_i)$, $(s_i)$ and $N$ be Euclidean switching data with $r_0$ even and $r_1$ odd. Then $2|s_1| < r_0$ or $2|s_2| < r_1 - 1$; that is, $|s_1| < r_0/2$ or $|s_2| < (r_1 - 1)/2$.

results.title: Endomorphism ring of a period lattice
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\omega_1, \omega_2$ be $\mathbb{R}$-linearly independent complex numbers with period lattice $\Lambda = \mathbb{Z}\omega_1 + \mathbb{Z}\omega_2$. The endomorphism ring of $\Lambda$ is the subring of $\mathbb{C}$ consisting of all $a \in \mathbb{C}$ such that $a z \in \Lambda$ for every $z \in \Lambda$.

results.title: Lattices that are proper ideals
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\Lambda$ be the period lattice of a pair of $\mathbb{R}$-linearly independent complex numbers, and let $\mathcal{O}$ be a subring of $\mathbb{C}$. Then $\Lambda$ is a proper ideal of $\mathcal{O}$ when the endomorphism ring of $\Lambda$, the subring of all $a \in \mathbb{C}$ with $a z \in \Lambda$ for every $z \in \Lambda$, equals $\mathcal{O}$.

results.title: Existence of the Cauchy principal value of $\varphi(x)/x$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every real-valued Schwartz function $\varphi$ on $\mathbb{R}$ there is a real number $L$ such that $\int_{\{x \in \mathbb{R} \,:\, |x| \ge \varepsilon\}} \varphi(x)/x \, dx \to L$ as $\varepsilon \to 0^+$, the integrals being taken with respect to Lebesgue measure.

results.title: The Dirac comb is a tempered distribution
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There is a tempered distribution $T$ on $\mathbb{R}$, that is, a continuous $\mathbb{C}$-linear functional on the space of complex-valued Schwartz functions on $\mathbb{R}$, such that $T(g)=\sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}} g(n)$ for every complex-valued Schwartz function $g$ on $\mathbb{R}$.

results.title: Path filtration
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $S$ be a measurable space. The path filtration on the path space $S^{\mathbb{N}}$ is the filtration indexed by $\mathbb{N}$, relative to the product σ-algebra, whose σ-algebra at time $n$ is the one generated by the coordinate maps $\omega \mapsto \omega_i$ for $i \le n$.

results.title: Vanishing of the cross terms in Wald's second equation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The full cross-term contribution to `E[(S_T)^2]` vanishes: `E[∑_{i < T} ∑_{j < i} X_j X_i] = 0` for identically distributed, mean-zero variables, with each `X_i` independent of the filtration at time `i` and measurable at time `i + 1`, given absolute summability of the stopped cross-term series.

results.title: Square of a finite sum as diagonal plus cross terms
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Algebraic identity expanding the square of a finite sum into diagonal and cross-term contributions: `(∑_{i<n} f i)^2 = ∑_{i<n} (f i)^2 + 2 ∑_{i<n} ∑_{j<i} f j · f i`.

results.title: Cross terms vanish for a bounded stopping time
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The total cross-term contribution vanishes for a stopping time bounded by a constant, with no extra summability or measurability hypotheses: the sums are finite, and every term past the bound is zero.

results.title: Integrability of the stopped sum in Wald's equation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Under Wald's hypotheses, the stopped sum is integrable. This reuses Wald's summable `L¹` series and applies Mathlib's sum measurability and norm bound.

results.title: Wald's equation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let `Xᵢ` be identically distributed integrable real random variables and `T` a stopping time with `E T < ∞`, with each `Xₖ` independent of the filtration at time `k`. Then `E[S_T] = E[X₁] · E[T]`, where `S_T = ∑_{i < T} Xᵢ`.

results.title: Integrability of the stopped sum of squares
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The stopped sum of squares is integrable under the stated diagonal hypotheses.

results.title: Diagonal identity in Wald's second equation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Wald's equation applied to the squared increments gives the diagonal identity.

results.title: Wald's second equation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $(\Omega, \mathbb{P})$ be a probability space with a filtration $(\mathcal{F}_k)_{k \ge 0}$, and let $X_0, X_1, \dots$ be identically distributed real random variables with $\mathbb{E}|X_0| < \infty$, $\mathbb{E}[X_0] = 0$ and $\mathbb{E}[X_0^2] < \infty$. results.title: Predictable filtration of a sequence
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The "predictable" filtration associated to a sequence `X : ℕ → Ω → ℝ`: `ℱ_k = σ(X_0, …, X_{k-1})`. Ported verbatim from v1 `WaldSecondEquation.lean`.

results.title: Predictable filtration at time zero is trivial
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The predictable filtration contains no observations at time zero.

results.title: Successor step of the predictable filtration
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A successor step adds exactly the next observation to the predictable filtration.

results.title: Square-integrability of a stopped partial sum
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Square-integrability of a stopped partial sum, general-filtration form.

results.title: Square-integrability of the maximal stopped partial sum
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Square-integrability of the maximal stopped partial sum, in v1's form: `max_{0 ≤ k ≤ T} Sₖ²` is integrable. This is v1's `integrable_maximal_stopped_partial_sum_sq`, whose proof in v1 was left unproved.

results.caption: Structure

results.title: Free $\mathbb{Z}^d$-action
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $d$ be a natural number, let $\mu$ be a measure on a measurable space $\Omega$, and let $T$ assign to each $v \in \mathbb{Z}^d$ a map $T_v \colon \Omega \to \Omega$. Then $T$ is free (in the Ornstein–Weiss sense) with respect to $\mu$ if, for every nonzero $v \in \mathbb{Z}^d$, the set of points $x \in \Omega$ with $T_v(x) = x$ has $\mu$-measure zero.

results.title: Integer box
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $d$ and $N$, the integer box $[0, N)^d$ is the finite set of vectors $v \in \mathbb{Z}^d$ with $0 \le v_i < N$ for every coordinate $i$.

results.title: Aperiodic transformation
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\mu$ be a measure on a measurable space $\Omega$. A map $T : \Omega \to \Omega$ is aperiodic with respect to $\mu$ if the set of periodic points of $T$, the points $x$ with $T^k(x) = x$ for some $k \ge 1$, where $T^k$ is the $k$-fold iterate of $T$, has (outer) $\mu$-measure zero. Equivalently, for $\mu$-almost every $x$, no positive iterate of $T$ fixes $x$.

results.title: Floor of a Rokhlin tower
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a map $T : \Omega \to \Omega$, a set $B \subseteq \Omega$ and $k \in \mathbb{N}$, the level-$k$ floor with base $B$ is the image $T^k(B)$ of $B$ under the $k$-fold iterate $T^k$ of $T$; the level-$0$ floor is $B$.

results.title: Union of a Rokhlin tower
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a map $T : \Omega \to \Omega$, a set $B \subseteq \Omega$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the union of the tower with base $B$ and height $n$ is the set $\bigcup_{k=0}^{n-1} T^k(B)$ of its floors $B, T(B), \dots, T^{n-1}(B)$, where $T^k(B)$ is the image of $B$ under the $k$-fold iterate of $T$. It is empty when $n = 0$, and no disjointness of the floors is required.

results.title: Rokhlin tower
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\Omega$ be a measurable space, $T : \Omega \to \Omega$ a map and $n \in \mathbb{N}$. A set $B \subseteq \Omega$ is the base of a Rokhlin tower of height $n$ for $T$ if $B$ is measurable and the floors $B, T(B), \dots, T^{n-1}(B)$ are pairwise disjoint, that is, $T^i(B) \cap T^j(B) = \emptyset$ for all $i \ne j$ with $i, j < n$; here $T^k(B)$ is the image of $B$ under the $k$-fold iterate of $T$.

results.title: Omega-limit set lies in every closed set containing the orbit
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The ω-limit set of a point under a semiflow is contained in every closed set that contains the forward orbit.

results.title: `V` is constant on the ω-limit set
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If the forward orbit of `x` lies in a compact set `K` and the continuous function `V` is nonincreasing along it, then there is a constant `c` (the limit of `V(ϕ t x)`) such that `V(ϕ t y) = c` for every `y ∈ ω⁺(x)` and every `t ≥ 0`.

results.title: The collision experiment
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a nonempty finite set $\alpha$ and a natural number $q$, the collision experiment is the probability distribution on $\{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$ obtained by drawing a function $s \colon \{0, \dots, q - 1\} \to \alpha$ uniformly at random (equivalently, $q$ independent uniform samples $s(0), \dots, s(q - 1)$ from $\alpha$) and outputting true exactly when $s$ is not injective, that is, when $s(i) = s(j)$…

results.title: Collision probability
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a nonempty finite set $\alpha$ and a natural number $q$, the collision probability is the probability, as a real number, that the collision experiment with $q$ samples from $\alpha$ outputs true, that is, that $q$ independent uniform samples from $\alpha$ contain two equal samples at distinct positions.

results.title: The exact collision probability
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a nonempty finite set with $N$ elements and $q$ a natural number. The probability that $q$ independent uniform samples from $\alpha$ contain a collision equals $1 - N (N - 1) \cdots (N - q + 1) / N^q$, where the product $N (N - 1) \cdots (N - q + 1)$ has $q$ factors (it is $1$ for $q = 0$ and $0$ for $q > N$).

results.title: Birthday upper bound
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a nonempty finite set with $N$ elements and $q$ a natural number. The probability that $q$ independent uniform samples from $\alpha$ contain a collision is at most $q (q - 1) / (2 N)$.

results.title: Birthday lower bound, exponential form
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a nonempty finite set with $N$ elements and $q$ a natural number. The probability that $q$ independent uniform samples from $\alpha$ contain a collision is at least $1 - \exp(-q (q - 1) / (2 N))$.

results.title: Birthday lower bound, rational form
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a nonempty finite set with $N$ elements, $q$ a natural number, and $x = q (q - 1) / (2 N)$. The probability that $q$ independent uniform samples from $\alpha$ contain a collision is at least $x / (1 + x)$.

results.title: Birthday lower bound
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a nonempty finite set with $N$ elements and $q$ a natural number with $q (q - 1) \le 2 N$. The probability that $q$ independent uniform samples from $\alpha$ contain a collision is at least $q (q - 1) / (4 N)$.

results.title: Birthday lower bound as stated in Katz and Lindell
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a nonempty finite set with $N$ elements and $q$ a natural number with $q \le \sqrt{2 N}$. The probability that $q$ independent uniform samples from $\alpha$ contain a collision is at least $q (q - 1) / (4 N)$.

results.title: Birthday lower bound for at most square-root many samples
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a nonempty finite set with $N$ elements and $q$ a natural number with $q \le \sqrt{N}$. The probability that $q$ independent uniform samples from $\alpha$ contain a collision is at least $q (q - 1) / (4 N)$.

results.title: Even odds of a collision
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a nonempty finite set with $N$ elements and $q$ a natural number with $2 N \le q (q - 1)$. The probability that $q$ independent uniform samples from $\alpha$ contain a collision is at least $1/2$.

results.caption: Inductive

results.title: Leaves of a dendrogram
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The leaves of a dendrogram, left to right.

results.title: Number of internal nodes of a dendrogram
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The number of internal (merge) nodes.

results.title: Leaf orderings of a dendrogram
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The leaf orders obtained by choosing, at each internal node, which child is drawn first. Each choice pattern contributes one entry, so the list has `2 ^ numInternal t` entries.

results.title: Adjacent-similarity score of a leaf order
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The score of a leaf order: the sum of the similarities of adjacent leaves.

results.title: Optimal leaf-ordering score
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The best score among the leaf orders of `t` (never `⊥`: `optScore_ne_bot`).

results.title: Optimal leaf-ordering score with fixed end leaves
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The best score among the leaf orders of `t` that start with `i` and end with `j` (`⊥` if there is none).

results.title: Joining two subtree orders at an adjacent leaf pair
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: One side of the recursion: the left part ranges over orders of a subtree with leaves `Ll` and best-score table `Ml`, the right part over a subtree with leaves `Lr` and table `Mr`; the two are joined at the adjacent pair `(k, l)`.

results.title: Bar-Joseph–Gifford–Jaakkola dynamic program for leaf ordering
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The dynamic program of Bar-Joseph, Gifford and Jaakkola: `bestEnds S t i j` is computed from the tables of the two children, trying both child orders.

results.title: A dendrogram with m internal nodes has $2^m$ leaf orders
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A dendrogram with `m` internal nodes has `2 ^ m` leaf orders (one per flip pattern).

results.title: Leaf orders are permutations of the leaves
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every leaf order of `t` is a permutation of its leaves.

results.title: Correctness of the optimal leaf ordering recursion
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Correctness of the optimal leaf ordering recursion (Bar-Joseph, Gifford and Jaakkola 2001): the dynamic program computes, for every end pair `(i, j)`, the best score of a leaf order of `t` starting at `i` and ending at `j`.

results.title: Optimal leaf-ordering score via the dynamic program
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The optimal leaf-ordering score is the best `bestEnds` value over end pairs of leaves.

results.title: Optimal leaf-ordering score is finite
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every dendrogram has a leaf order, so the optimal score is a real number.
